why: An alternating substring must match one of two fixed patterns, 0101... or 1010.... Against a fixed pattern each mismatch costs one flip, so this is the longest window with at most k mismatches, run once per pattern.
hints: There are only two alternating strings of any length: one starting with 0 and one starting with 1, aligned to position parity.
Fix one target pattern. A position needs a flip if music[i] differs from the target at i. Now you want the longest window containing at most k such positions.
For each of the two targets, slide a window, counting mismatches and shrinking from the left while the count exceeds k. Take the best length. O(n).
pitfalls: Try both patterns; the best one may start with either 0 or 1.
k = 0 still allows the longest alternating run that already exists.
If k is at least the window's mismatches, the whole string can be the answer.
constraints:
• 1 ≤ |music| ≤ 10^5 (not stated in the source)
  • 0 ≤ k ≤ |music| (not stated in the source)
  • music contains only '0' and '1'
